title: Gaokao English
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public Gaokao English syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A notice at the village clinic states that it opens at eight in the morning and closes at six in the evening from Monday to Friday, but on Saturday it closes at noon. What time does the clinic close on Saturday?
items.explanation: The notice gives noon as the Saturday closing time and six in the evening only on weekdays, so the other times do not apply to Saturday.

items.stem: A passage describes how a delta town planted mangroves, rebuilt sand dunes and raised a sea wall, and reports that flood damage fell by more than half in six years. What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Mangroves grow faster than sand dunes.
Combining several defences reduced flood damage.
A sea wall is the cheapest single defence.
The town gave up protecting its coast.
items.explanation: The passage lists three measures working together and reports a large fall in flood damage, so its main idea is that combining defences cut the damage.

items.stem: A report says the new high-speed line opened only two months ago yet has already carried more passengers than it was expected to carry in its whole first year. What can be inferred from the report?
options: The line will be closed next year.
Tickets were given away without charge.
The line is more popular than its planners expected.
The planners set no passenger target.
items.explanation: Beating a full first-year target within two months shows demand is higher than the planners forecast, so the line is more popular than expected.

items.stem: A museum guide states that the porcelain gallery is on the third floor, the sculpture gallery is on the second floor and the cafe is on the ground floor. On which floor is the porcelain gallery to be found?
items.explanation: The guide places the porcelain gallery on the third floor, while the sculpture gallery is on the second floor and the cafe is on the ground floor.

items.stem: A researcher writes that the evidence for the claim is scant because it rests on a single small trial with only twelve participants. As used here, the word scant most nearly means which of the following?
items.explanation: The single small trial makes the evidence too thin to support the claim, so scant means insufficient rather than abundant, recent or convincing.

items.stem: An article lists the additives in a popular drink, explains what each one is used for and warns that two of them may trigger reactions in some consumers. What is the writer's main purpose?
options: To persuade readers to buy the drink
To inform readers about the drink's additives
To describe the factory that makes the drink
items.explanation: The article explains what each additive does and warns of possible reactions, so its purpose is to inform readers about those additives.

items.stem: A weather bulletin predicts heavy snow on Monday, clear skies on Tuesday and gale-force winds on Wednesday. According to the bulletin, on which day are gale-force winds expected?
items.explanation: The bulletin links gale-force winds to Wednesday, while Monday brings heavy snow and Tuesday is described as clear.

items.stem: A manager's email praises the team for meeting every delivery deadline this quarter but notes that three major clients have not yet renewed their contracts. What does the email suggest?
options: Strong delivery performance alone does not secure renewals.
All the major clients have already renewed.
items.explanation: Meeting every deadline yet facing three unrenewed contracts suggests that strong delivery does not by itself guarantee client renewals.

items.stem: A passage explains that bees, hoverflies, moths and some small birds all transfer pollen, and that removing any one group can lower fruit yields. What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why bees are the only useful pollinators
The value of several different pollinators
items.explanation: The passage names several pollinator groups and says losing any one lowers yields, so its main point is the value of many different pollinators.

items.stem: A geography text states that the river rises in the northern hills, passes through the industrial city of Wuxi and finally empties into the sea. According to the text, which place does the river pass through?
items.explanation: The text says the river flows through Wuxi after leaving the northern hills and before reaching the sea, so Wuxi is the place it passes through.

items.stem: A reviewer says the scenery of the new film is breathtaking but its plot is so thin that the reviewer looked at the clock twice. What is the reviewer's overall view?
items.explanation: Praising the scenery while criticising the thin plot gives a mixed view in which the visuals are admired but the story is weak.

items.stem: A study finds that pupils who walked to school arrived more alert than those who came by car, although both groups reported the same number of hours of sleep. What does this suggest?
options: Sleep has no effect on alertness.
Being driven to school is healthier.
items.explanation: With sleep held constant, the alertness advantage of the walkers points to morning exercise rather than sleep as the likely cause.

items.stem: A passage describes how a crowded city turned unused roofs into gardens that cool the buildings, soak up rainwater and supply fresh vegetables. What is the passage mainly about?
options: The cost of building new parks
The history of one city family
The dangers of growing food in cities
items.explanation: The passage lists cooling, rainwater absorption and fresh food as advantages of rooftop gardens, so those benefits are its main subject.

items.stem: A swimming pool leaflet says the pool is open from six in the morning until ten at night on weekdays and from eight in the morning until six in the evening at weekends. At what time does the pool close on Sunday?
items.explanation: The leaflet gives weekend hours of eight in the morning until six in the evening, so on Sunday the pool closes at six in the evening.

items.stem: A text warns that the old footbridge is dilapidated and that inspectors now fear it may collapse under heavy loads. As used here, the word dilapidated means which of the following?
items.explanation: Inspectors fearing a collapse shows the bridge is badly worn, so dilapidated means in a state of disrepair rather than safe or admired.

items.stem: Choose the sentence that is grammatically correct in standard written English.
options: She has lived in Beijing since five years.
She is living in Beijing since 2019.
She has lived in Beijing since 2019.
items.explanation: The present perfect has lived pairs with since plus a point in time, so the other options mix tenses that do not fit the time phrase.

items.stem: Complete the sentence with the correct word. The committee has not yet reached ______ final decision on the matter.
items.explanation: The committee is treated here as a single body, so the singular possessive its is correct, while their would require a plural subject.

items.stem: Complete the sentence with the correct preposition. Regular practice will make you better ______ solving such problems.
items.explanation: The adjective better takes the preposition at before a gerund, giving better at solving, while the other prepositions do not fit this pattern.

items.stem: Choose the word that is closest in meaning to the word reluctant in the sentence. The manager was reluctant to approve the unusual request.
items.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant, so unwilling is the closest synonym, while eager and delighted are close to its opposite.

items.stem: Choose the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to the word generous in the sentence. He was generous with both his time and his money.
items.explanation: Generous means giving freely, so its opposite is stingy, while kind, helpful and ample do not carry the opposite meaning.

items.stem: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form. If I ______ more free time, I would take up painting.
items.explanation: This is a second conditional about an unreal present, so the if-clause takes the past simple had and the main clause takes would.

items.stem: Complete the sentence with the correct relative pronoun. The novel, ______ was published last spring, has already been translated.
items.explanation: Which is the correct relative pronoun for a thing, the novel, while who is used for people and what cannot introduce this kind of clause.

items.stem: Complete the sentence with the correct preposition. The whole class apologised ______ arriving so late.
items.explanation: The verb apologise is followed by for plus a gerund, so for arriving is the correct form in this sentence.

items.stem: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement.
options: The list of candidates were posted yesterday.
The list of candidates have been posted.
The list of candidates are posted.
The list of candidates was posted yesterday.
items.explanation: The subject is list, which is singular, so the verb must be was, since the phrase of candidates does not change the number of the subject.

items.stem: Complete the sentence with the correct modal verb. Passengers ______ fasten their seat belts before the plane takes off, since the rule is compulsory.
items.explanation: A compulsory rule expresses obligation, which must conveys, while might and could express possibility and would rather expresses preference.

items.stem: Complete the sentence with the correct tense. By the time the guests arrived, the host ______ the whole meal.
items.explanation: The past perfect had cooked marks the earlier of two past events, which fits the meal being ready before the guests arrived.

items.stem: Complete the sentence with the correct quantifier. There is ______ water left in the bottle, so we should buy some more.
items.explanation: Water is uncountable, so it takes little, while few, many and several are used with countable nouns instead.

items.stem: Choose the correct adverb to complete the sentence. Although she has studied for years, she still speaks German ______.
items.explanation: The verb speaks is modified by an adverb, so fluently is correct rather than the adjective fluent or a noun form.

items.stem: Choose the word that best completes the collocation. The two governments finally agreed to ______ a decision about the border.
items.explanation: English collocates decision with make, as in to make a decision, while do, take and give do not form this fixed phrase.

items.stem: Complete the second conditional sentence. If it ______ tomorrow, the sports meeting would be postponed.
items.explanation: The main clause uses would be postponed, so the if-clause takes the past simple rained to form a second conditional.

items.stem: Read the sentence and choose the best word for the blank. Although the path was steep and rocky, the hikers kept ______ until they reached the summit.
items.explanation: The verb keep takes a gerund, so kept climbing is correct, while the infinitive and bare forms do not fit this pattern.

items.stem: Read the sentence and choose the best word for the blank. The ancient temple, ______ walls are covered with paintings, attracts thousands of visitors each year.
items.explanation: The blank shows possession of the walls, so the possessive relative pronoun whose is required rather than who, which or that.

items.stem: Read the passage and choose the best word for the blank. For centuries the Silk Road carried goods between East and West, and along it ideas and inventions travelled ______, shaping many distant cultures.
items.explanation: The phrase as well means also, which fits ideas travelling alongside goods, while the other options are unrelated in meaning.

items.stem: Read the sentence and choose the best word for the blank. Hardly ______ the meeting begun when the power failed and the room went dark.
items.explanation: Hardly had plus the past participle forms the inverted past perfect pattern, so had is required before the meeting begun.

items.stem: Read the sentence and choose the best word for the blank. The young engineer was praised not only for her skill but also for her ______ to work long hours when the project needed her.
items.explanation: The possessive her requires a noun, so willingness is correct, while willing is an adjective and willingly is an adverb.

items.stem: Read the sentence and choose the best word for the blank. The scientist repeated the experiment several times ______ she could be certain that the result was reliable.
items.explanation: The clause states the purpose of repeating the experiment, so the purpose connector so that is correct rather than a contrast or condition.

items.stem: Read the passage and choose the best word for the blank. Bamboo grows faster than almost any other plant, and for this ______ it is widely used in construction, furniture and even clothing.
items.explanation: The fast growth explains the wide use, and the fixed phrase for this reason introduces that explanation, so reason is correct.

items.stem: Read the sentence and choose the best word for the blank. We had no sooner sat down at the table ______ the waiter brought the menu.
items.explanation: The fixed pattern no sooner is followed by than, so than completes the sentence, while when and that do not fit this structure.

items.stem: Read the sentence and choose the best word for the blank. The professor suggested that every student ______ a short essay before the end of the term.
items.explanation: After suggest that, English uses the base form write in the subjunctive, so the other verb forms do not fit this construction.

items.stem: Read the sentence and choose the best word for the blank. Not until the lights went out ______ how much the audience had enjoyed the performance.
items.explanation: When the negative phrase not until begins the sentence the subject and auxiliary invert, so realised the actors is the correct order.

items.stem: Read the sentence and choose the best word for the blank. The river is too wide and deep ______ on foot, so the villagers built a small wooden bridge.
items.explanation: The pattern too wide and deep to cross uses the infinitive to express that crossing is impossible, so to cross is correct.

items.stem: Read the sentence and choose the best word for the blank. The teacher advised us to look ______ the word in the dictionary if we did not know its meaning.
items.explanation: The phrasal verb look up means to search for information in a reference work, so up fits consulting a dictionary.

items.stem: Read the passage and choose the best word for the blank. Many desert animals stay underground during the hottest hours and come out only at night, ______ they can avoid the fierce heat of the day.
items.explanation: Coming out at night is a means of avoiding the heat, so the purpose connector so that fits, while the others mark contrast or concession.

items.stem: Read the sentence and choose the best word for the blank. It was not the prize ______ pleased him but the respect of his colleagues.
items.explanation: The emphatic pattern it was not the prize needs the word that to introduce the clause, while what and which do not fit this structure.

items.stem: Read the sentence and choose the best word for the blank. The more carefully you plan your revision, ______ anxious you will feel on the day of the examination.
items.explanation: The parallel comparison the more requires the less in the second clause, so the less anxious is the correct form.

items.stem: A student wants to link two contrasting ideas in one sentence. Which transition best fills the blank? The plan was expensive; ______, it was the only one that solved the problem.
items.explanation: The second clause contrasts with the first, so the contrast transition however is correct, while therefore, moreover and likewise signal other relationships.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: Which sentence best serves as the topic sentence of a paragraph arguing that school sport improves academic focus?
options: Many schools in the region have large playing fields.
Regular sport can improve pupils' concentration in class.
Some pupils dislike running long distances.
Our school has recently bought new equipment.
items.explanation: A topic sentence states the paragraph's main claim, so the sentence linking sport to concentration fits, while the others give minor detail.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: Choose the most appropriate concluding sentence for a letter applying for a summer course. The student has explained her background, described her reasons for applying and listed her achievements.
options: I do not really expect to hear from you.
The course fee is far too high for anyone.
I would be grateful for the chance to join the course.
I have forgotten why I started this letter.
items.explanation: A closing for an application should be polite and forward-looking, so the sentence expressing gratitude for a chance to join is most appropriate.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
options: Although it rained we still went out.
Although, it rained we still went out.
Although it rained, we still went, out.
Although it rained, we still went out.
items.explanation: A subordinate clause at the start of a sentence is followed by a comma before the main clause, so only the correctly punctuated form is right.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: A writer wants to make a formal complaint to a hotel manager. Which opening is most appropriate in register?
options: I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with my recent stay.
Your hotel is a total disaster, honestly.
Hey, guess what happened to me last week.
I want to tell you something about your staff.
items.explanation: A formal complaint needs polite, neutral wording, so the sentence stating dissatisfaction in measured language fits best, unlike the casual options.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: Which sentence best summarises the paragraph without losing its main point? The paragraph explains that early railways were slow, dangerous and expensive, yet within fifty years they had replaced most road transport.
options: Despite early problems, railways quickly transformed transport.
Road transport disappeared forever in one year.
Railways were cheap from the day they opened.
items.explanation: A good summary keeps the paragraph's contrast between early problems and rapid change, which the sentence about transforming transport captures.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: A paragraph about air pollution is meant to persuade readers to use public transport. Which sentence would best support that purpose?
options: Buses and trains produce far less pollution per passenger.
Public transport can occasionally be delayed.
items.explanation: To persuade readers towards public transport, the strongest support is evidence of its lower pollution, while the other sentences are irrelevant or discouraging.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: Which linking word best fills the blank? The museum was free to enter; ______, it was crowded every weekend.
items.explanation: Free entry leads naturally to weekend crowds, so the result connector consequently is correct, while the other options signal different relationships.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: A student is editing an essay and finds the sentence The reason why the project failed was because the budget was too small. Which revision removes the redundancy?
options: The project failed because the budget was too small.
The reason why the project failed was due to the reason of a small budget.
The reason the project failed was because of the small budget it had.
The project failed for the reason that the budget was because small.
items.explanation: The original repeats the idea of cause through both reason and because, so the concise revision using a single because removes the redundancy.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: Which sentence uses the most appropriate cohesive device to add information? The new library is spacious; ______, it is equipped with modern computers.
items.explanation: The second clause adds a further positive feature, so the addition connector moreover is correct, while the other options signal contrast or replacement.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: A writer wants to soften a criticism of a classmate's draft. Which comment is most constructive?
options: This draft is a hopeless mess.
I cannot understand why you bother writing.
The ideas are clear, and reordering the paragraphs would make them stronger.
There is nothing worth keeping here.
items.explanation: Constructive criticism balances praise with a specific suggestion, so the comment noting clear ideas and a way to improve is most helpful.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: Which sentence best expresses the conclusion of a report that studied three possible sites and chose the second?
options: All three sites are equally unsuitable.
The study examined only one site.
We recommend no site at all.
After comparing the sites, we recommend the second.
items.explanation: A conclusion states the outcome of the study, so the sentence comparing the sites and recommending the second correctly reports the chosen one.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: Choose the transition that best fills the blank. She had trained for months; ______, she won the race with ease.
items.explanation: Months of training explain the easy win, so the result connector as a result fits, while the other transitions signal contrast or example.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: Which sentence most clearly states the writer's opinion about school uniforms in an argumentative paragraph?
options: Uniforms are made of cloth and come in several sizes.
Some schools do not require uniforms at all.
School uniforms give everyone a sense of belonging and reduce cost.
Uniforms can be bought from many different shops.
items.explanation: An argumentative paragraph needs a clear position, so the sentence claiming uniforms build belonging and cut cost states an opinion, unlike the factual options.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse

items.stem: A summary should keep the main points and leave out minor detail. Which sentence is the best summary of a passage stating that sleep improves memory, mood and physical health?
options: The passage mentions that people use pillows.
The passage describes one person's bedtime routine.
The passage says nothing important about sleep.
The passage explains that sleep benefits memory, mood and health.
items.explanation: A summary must capture the central claims, so the sentence listing the three benefits of sleep summarises the passage without adding minor detail.
items.reference: Gaokao English Syllabus - Writing and Discourse
